Method of Attack: Speculative execution side-channel data-sampling attacks leaking data from CPU buffers
RIDL exploits bugs in Intel CPU internal buffers (Line-Fill Buffers, Load Ports) to leak data
Fallout exploits Store Buffers vulnerability to leak data, bypassing KASLR
ZombieLoad exploits Fill Buffers vulnerability to leak secrets from other running programs
Discoverer: VUSec (Vrije University Amsterdam and CISPA) for RIDL
University of Michigan, University of Adelaide, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, Data61, Graz IAIK, KU Leuven for Fallout
Not explicitly stated for ZombieLoad but related to RIDL researchers
Impacted Systems: Intel CPUs released since 2008 including 9th generation processors
Cloud computing resources and virtual machines
Systems running Linux (e.g., /etc/shadow, /proc/version) and SGX enclaves
Attack Vector: Running unprivileged malicious code on vulnerable Intel CPUs
Malicious JavaScript on webpages or advertisements
Shared cloud computing resources or virtual machines
Indicators of Compromise: Videos demonstrating data leaks from /etc/shadow, /proc/version, and via JavaScript
Security advisories and microcode updates from Intel
